description:
Finding: The boundary between validate() and main.rs startup guards is inconsistently drawn.

validate() already contains a security guard with no I/O: the allow_http+credential cleartext check in reader/config.rs (lines 637-655 and 700-719). Yet the dev-mode loopback guard (is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr()) and the signing_key_path guard live in main.rs, also without any I/O dependency.

The stated split — validate() for structure, main.rs for runtime — is not consistently applied. A reader of validate() cannot rely on it being the complete set of config-time security invariants, because some are checked later in main.rs. This creates a gap: --check-config (if ever added) would pass validate() but miss the loopback guard.

Suggested fix: move the pure-logic security guards (is_dev_mode+loopback, signing_key_path+loopback) into validate() alongside the existing allow_http guard, reserving main.rs guards for checks that require actual I/O (Kubo ping, file readability, cert expiry).
title: dev-mode guard split: validate() vs main.rs is inconsistent
